parts.name: shell body

physics.Basic_description: Large white spherical shell with a smooth, matte finish, forming the main enclosure of the helmet.
physics.Functional_description: Provides structural integrity and protection for the astronaut's head against vacuum and debris.
physics.Grasped_description: Grasp the upper curvature of the shell firmly with parallel jaws, avoiding the visor area.
physics.reason: The shell is a thin-walled pressure vessel enclosing a large air volume; treating it as solid would vastly overestimate mass.

parts.name: interior lip

physics.Basic_description: Grey textured padding visible inside the face opening, appearing soft and porous.
physics.Functional_description: Cushions the face and provides a seal against the skin for comfort and pressure retention.
physics.Grasped_description: Not suitable for grasping due to softness and internal location.
physics.reason: Foam padding is effectively a solid block of low-density material relative to the scale of the object.

parts.name: neck seat

physics.Basic_description: Grey metallic ring with vertical ridges at the base of the helmet, appearing machined.
physics.Functional_description: Interface ring for locking the helmet to the spacesuit torso.
physics.Grasped_description: Grasp the ridged outer edge of the ring for a secure hold during manipulation.
physics.reason: Machined metal ring is a thin-walled cylinder, not a solid block of aluminum.

parts.name: port 0

physics.Basic_description: Small magenta cylindrical protrusion on the side of the helmet shell.
physics.Functional_description: Connection point for hoses, lights, or communication gear.
physics.Grasped_description: Too small to support the weight of the object; avoid grasping.
physics.reason: Port is a hollow connector housing, not a solid rod.

parts.description: Small magenta cylindrical protrusion on the side of the helmet shell.

parts.name: neck collar

physics.Basic_description: Pinkish-white lower rim surrounding the neck opening, smooth plastic finish.
physics.Functional_description: Structural base of the helmet shell that mates with the neck ring.
physics.Grasped_description: Can be grasped by the rim if the shell body is obstructed, though less stable.
physics.reason: Extension of the main shell wall, enclosing air.

parts.description: Pinkish-white lower rim surrounding the neck opening, smooth plastic finish.

parts.name: visor frame

physics.Basic_description: Lime-green curved frame surrounding the visor bubble, matching the shell material.
physics.Functional_description: Holds the visor bubble in place and provides the pivot mechanism housing.
physics.Grasped_description: Grasp the top arch of the frame to lift or rotate the helmet carefully.
physics.reason: Frame is a structural shell component, hollow inside to save weight.

parts.description: Lime-green curved frame surrounding the visor bubble, matching the shell material.

parts.name: visor bubble

physics.Basic_description: Teal-tinted transparent curved shield covering the face opening, glossy surface.
physics.Functional_description: Protects the eyes from solar radiation and provides visibility.
physics.Grasped_description: Do not grasp; surface is slippery and prone to scratching or cracking under point load.
physics.reason: Visor is a thin curved sheet of plastic, definitely not a solid block.

parts.description: Teal-tinted transparent curved shield covering the face opening, glossy surface.

parts.name: pivot knob 0

physics.Basic_description: Small brown circular knob at the pivot point of the visor frame.
physics.Functional_description: Allows the user to lock or unlock the visor rotation.
physics.Grasped_description: Can be pinched to rotate, but too small to lift the whole object.
physics.reason: Small knob is likely a solid molded piece or filled with mechanism, approximated as solid.

simulation.collision: CoACD convex decomposition of concave source collision meshes (relative tolerance 0.03–0.05)

collisionFilter.description: Self-contact excluded between directly connected rigid groups, including the fixed base; nonadjacent contacts retained

simulation.inertia: Source URDF link inertials; missing inertials use geometry-derived defaults (density 1000 kg/m³)
simulation.friction: Source URDF mu1 as sliding friction; torsional 0.005, rolling 0.0001
simulation.contact: MuJoCo soft contacts (solref 0.01 1); source restitution is displayed, not converted
simulation.material: Rigid bodies; Young’s modulus and Poisson ratio are annotations, not soft-body parameters

interaction.description: Switchable virtual joint damping and reflected armature for interactive inspection; source properties are unchanged.
interaction.rule: damping ≥ rated effort / rated speed; armature = 2% child subtree mass (slide) or 2% mass × collision radius² (hinge)
